title: Fibre products and equalizers in fibred groupoids
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$, with functors over the base as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. A fibre product means an ordinary categorical pullback in the total category: maps into it are pairs of maps with equal composites. An equalizer of parallel arrows $r,s:x\to y$ means an arrow $e:z\to x$ such that $re=se$ and every $t:w\to x$ with $rt=st$ factors uniquely through $e$. Then $\mathcal C$ has fibre products, and every functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ preserves them. If $\mathcal C$ is an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], then its total category has equalizers. If $\mathcal C$ has equalizers and $F$ is faithful, meaning that every map on Hom sets is injective, then $F$ preserves equalizers.

proof.text: Write $p:\mathcal C\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ and $q:\mathcal D\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ for the projections. Given $a:x\to y$ and $b:z\to y$, form $P=p(x)\times_{p(y)}p(z)$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]; its structural map to $S$ is the common composite of its projections. By [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], choose $c:w\to z$ over $P\to p(z)$. Every arrow is strongly cartesian in the explicit sense of [lem-sfb-cartesian-lift-pullback-square]. Apply that node to $a,b,c$: it supplies $d:w\to x$ over the other projection and proves that $(d,c)$ is an ordinary categorical pullback of $a,b$. This proves existence in $\mathcal C$.

Apply $F$ to the square constructed in step 1. Since $qF=p$, its base square is still the pullback $P$. Every arrow of $\mathcal D$ is strongly cartesian by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Thus [lem-sfb-cartesian-lift-pullback-square] applied to $F(a),F(b),F(c)$ proves that its upper arrow is $F(d)$ (the defining composite and base map coincide), and that this image square is a pullback. For any other pullback cone of $a,b$, the universal properties give comparison maps to and from $(w,d,c)$; both composites are identities because their composites with both projections agree with the identity. Applying $F$ preserves these inverse comparisons, and hence its image cone is a pullback too. Therefore $F$ preserves all fibre products, not just the choices of step 1.

source.place: Tag 06WZ, lemma-fibre-products-morphism (1), with independence of pullback choices expanded

proof.text: If $\mathcal C$ is an algebraic stack, [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-total-equalizers] gives an equalizer for every pair of parallel arrows in its total category. Its hypotheses are precisely the universes, scheme base, fibred-groupoid structure and algebraic-stack hypothesis in the present statement. In particular this covers parallel arrows lying over different base maps, with no extra separatedness hypothesis.

For the remaining assertion assume $F$ faithful and let $e:z\to x$ equalize $r,s:x\to y$ universally. The arrow $e$ is monic: if $eu=ev$, then $u,v$ are two factorizations through $e$ of the same arrow equalizing $r,s$, and so $u=v$. Consequently the cone $(\mathrm{id}_z,\mathrm{id}_z)$ is a pullback of $e$ with itself: a cone $(u,v)$ satisfies $eu=ev$, hence $u=v$, and has unique mediating arrow $u$. By step 2 its image $(\mathrm{id}_{Fz},\mathrm{id}_{Fz})$ is also a pullback. For arrows $u,v:t\to Fz$ with $F(e)u=F(e)v$, its mediating arrow must equal both $u$ and $v$. Thus $F(e)$ is monic.

source.place: Tag 06WZ, lemma-fibre-products-morphism (2), uniqueness detail via part (1)

proof.text: Let $t:w\to F(x)$ equalize $F(r),F(s)$ and put $h=q(t):q(w)\to p(x)$. Choose a lift $c:x_h\to x$ over $h$ using [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. The arrows $F(c)$ and $t$ have the same target and base arrow. Their cartesian universal properties give arrows $\alpha:w\to F(x_h)$ and $\beta:F(x_h)\to w$ over the identity, with $F(c)\alpha=t$ and $t\beta=F(c)$; the same uniqueness gives $\alpha\beta=\mathrm{id}$ and $\beta\alpha=\mathrm{id}$. Therefore $F(rc)\alpha=F(r)t=F(s)t=F(sc)\alpha$, and cancellation of $\alpha$ followed by faithfulness gives $rc=sc$. The equalizer property of $e$ supplies $l:x_h\to z$ with $el=c$. Then $v=F(l)\alpha:w\to F(z)$ satisfies $F(e)v=t$.

source.place: Tag 06WZ, lemma-fibre-products-morphism (2), cartesian-lift existence argument expanded

proof.text: Functoriality gives $F(r)F(e)=F(s)F(e)$. Every equalizing arrow $t$ has a factor $v$ by step 5, and any two factors are equal because $F(e)$ is monic by step 4. This is the ordinary equalizer universal property, so $F$ preserves equalizers whenever they exist in $\mathcal C$.
